---
title: "Common Cargo Commands"
---

Cargo is Rust's build tool **and** package manager in one. If you know the .NET CLI, it maps closely: `cargo` is to Rust what `dotnet` is to C#.

## Project anatomy

```
cargo new hello_rust
        │
        ▼
hello_rust/
├── Cargo.toml        ← manifest (like .csproj / pubspec.yaml / pyproject.toml)
├── Cargo.lock        ← exact resolved versions (auto-generated)
├── .gitignore        ← git repo initialized for you
├── src/
│   └── main.rs       ← entry point (binary crate)
│                       (lib.rs for a library crate)
└── target/           ← build output (git-ignored)
    ├── debug/        ← `cargo build`
    └── release/      ← `cargo build --release`
```

## 1. Creating projects

```bash
cargo new my_app            # new binary (executable) project
cargo new my_lib --lib      # new library project (src/lib.rs)
cargo init                  # turn the current folder into a Cargo project
```

## 2. Building & running

```bash
cargo check                 # type-check only, no binary → FASTEST feedback loop
cargo build                 # debug build    → target/debug/my_app
cargo build --release       # optimized build → target/release/my_app
cargo run                   # build + run
cargo run --release         # build optimized + run
cargo run -- --input a.txt  # args after `--` go to YOUR program, not Cargo
cargo clean                 # delete target/ folder
```

> 💡 `cargo check` is what you'll run most. It skips code generation, so it's much faster than `build`. Debug builds can be 10–100× slower at runtime than release builds, so always benchmark with `--release`.

## 3. Dependencies (crates from crates.io)

```bash
cargo add serde                       # add latest version to Cargo.toml
cargo add serde --features derive     # with a feature flag
cargo add tokio@1.40                  # specific version
cargo add --dev pretty_assertions     # dev-only dependency (tests)
cargo remove serde                    # remove a dependency
cargo update                          # update Cargo.lock within semver ranges
cargo tree                            # show the dependency tree
```

Which writes into `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[package]
name = "my_app"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }

[dev-dependencies]
pretty_assertions = "1.4"
```

## 4. Testing & benchmarking

```bash
cargo test                       # run all tests (unit + integration + doc tests)
cargo test parse                 # run only tests whose name contains "parse"
cargo test -- --nocapture        # show println! output from tests
cargo test --release             # test with optimizations
cargo bench                      # run benchmarks
```

## 5. Code quality (your "clean code" toolkit)

```bash
cargo fmt                   # auto-format code (like black / dart format)
cargo fmt --check           # verify formatting only (good for CI)
cargo clippy                # linter with ~700 lints and helpful suggestions
cargo clippy -- -D warnings # treat warnings as errors (CI)
cargo doc --open            # generate HTML docs from /// comments and open in browser
```

> 💡 Clippy is like having a Rust mentor review your code. It often teaches you idiomatic Rust ("this loop could be an iterator", "this clone is unnecessary").

## 6. Installing tools & publishing

```bash
cargo install ripgrep        # install a Rust CLI tool globally (~/.cargo/bin)
cargo install --list         # list installed tools
cargo publish                # publish your crate to crates.io
```

## Typical daily workflow

```
 ┌──────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌────────────┐    ┌────────────────────┐
 │ edit .rs │───▶│ cargo check │───▶│ cargo clippy │───▶│ cargo test │───▶│ cargo build        │
 └──────────┘    └─────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └────────────┘    │   --release        │
      ▲               │ errors?                                           └────────────────────┘
      └───────────────┘   (Rust compiler errors are very descriptive — read them!)
```

## Rosetta stone with tools you already know

| Task | Rust (Cargo) | C# (.NET) | Dart | Python (uv) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New project | `cargo new` | `dotnet new console` | `dart create` | `uv init` |
| Add package | `cargo add` | `dotnet add package` | `dart pub add` | `uv add` |
| Build | `cargo build` | `dotnet build` | `dart compile exe` | n/a |
| Run | `cargo run` | `dotnet run` | `dart run` | `uv run` |
| Test | `cargo test` | `dotnet test` | `dart test` | `uv run pytest` |
| Format | `cargo fmt` | `dotnet format` | `dart format` | `ruff format` |
| Lint | `cargo clippy` | Roslyn analyzers | `dart analyze` | `ruff check` |
| Manifest | `Cargo.toml` | `.csproj` | `pubspec.yaml` | `pyproject.toml` |
| Lockfile | `Cargo.lock` | `packages.lock.json` | `pubspec.lock` | `uv.lock` |

## Bonus: workspace flag

When you have a multi-crate **workspace** (like a .NET solution with several projects), target a specific member with `-p`:

```bash
cargo build -p core_lib
cargo test  -p api_server
```
